audit.reasoning: Coding (fixed-dominant penultimate, non-strict because of the stressed vocative) is correct and is now independently confirmed by Launey 1986:532-533 (vocatives are 'les seuls oxytons de la langue nahuatl'; men's -é accented suffix; women's vocative = shift of accent 'de la pénultième à la dernière syllabe') and by Carochi 1645 Lib.1 cap.3 §1 (vocative e 'con accento agudo, y en tono alto'). But the record's deciding citation is an uncited Wikipedia section, with empty quote/cite/loc/grade fields, for a language with 39 Glottolog descriptive refs including 400-1600 pp grammars. Action: re-cite the record to Launey 1986 §5.1.2.5 pp. 532-533 (now, scanned in scanned/ and) with Carochi 1645 as older-primary support, and upgrade to Launey 2011 / Andrews 2003 when obtainable. No recode needed.
audit.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK (agree: no-held-file, verbatim to Wikipedia). 'held' is empty; the record's only source is Wikipedia 'Classical Nahuatl' §Accent. The saved wikitext line 103 reads 'Stress generally falls on the penultimate syllable. The one exception is the vocative suffix (used by men) -é, which is added to the end of a word and is always stressed' -- matches the record text; the section carries no <ref>. sources.quote: Stress generally falls on the penultimate syllable. The one exception is the vocative suffix (used by men) -e, which is added to the end of a word and is always stressed.

sources.citation: Launey, Michel. 1986. Catégories et opérations dans la grammaire nahuatl. Thèse de Doctorat d'État, Université de Paris IV. vii+1609 pp. (CNRS-CELIA online edition, via web.archive.org)
sources.quote: p.532: 'les formes vocatives constituent d'un point de vue accentuel les seuls oxytons de la langue nahuatl' ... 'Le vocatif utilisé par un homme est en effet marqué par un suffixe accentué /-é/'; p.533: 'tandis que le vocatif utilisé par une femme est marqué par un simple déplacement de l'accent de la pénultième à la dernière syllabe' ... 'aucun dialecte moderne n'utilise à notre connaissance de vocatif oxyton'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Classical Nahuatl', §Accent (wikitext fetched sources 2026-09-16)
sources.quote: 'Stress generally falls on the penultimate syllable. The one exception is the vocative suffix (used by men) -é ... always stressed' + 'When women use the vocative, the stress is shifted to the final syllable without adding any suffix.' No citation attached.

sources.citation: Carochi, Horacio. 1645. Arte de la lengua mexicana con la declaración de los adverbios della. México: Juan Ruyz. (archive.org item artedelalenguame00caro, scanned text)
sources.quote: Vocative: 'forman los varones el vocativo añadiendo una e pronunciada con accento agudo, y en tono alto' ... 'Las mugeres no usan desta e en el Vocativo pero levantan mucho la postrera syllaba del nombre'. Accents chapter treats vowel length and saltillo; notes final long syllables are pronounced 'en tono baxo como todas las demás syllabas finales largas' (consistent with non-final prominence) but states no general penult rule.
sources.locator: Libro primero, cap. 3 §1 'Del vocativo' (f. 8); cap. 1 §'De los accentos'
